title: Make all Atelier tool surfaces parallel-agent safe and Argus steerable
operator_request: Everything should be usable by parallel agents inside Handshake, with front-end and back-end navigation paths and Argus visual proof; missing GUI/operator surfaces are accepted scope expansion.

state_recovery.recovery_rule: Audit every Atelier surface for stable IDs, routes, leases, receipts, and visual proof. Treat gaps as product debt, not documentation-only issues.

scope.summary: Harden CKC, Posekit, Ingest, Facial-backed tools, and prompt feedback surfaces for safe parallel model operation.
base_scope: Audit stable author_id coverage for all Atelier tabs, controls, lists, viewers, and status regions.
Add deterministic backend/headless commands where GUI-only operation blocks agents.
Add receipts/attribution for model actions that mutate CKC/Posekit/Ingest state.
Ensure parallel agents have leases/conflict behavior for shared mutable targets.
Expose enough structured state for no-context recovery.
Update internal UserManual with model operation rules.
acceptance_criteria: Every major Atelier surface has stable Argus-visible author_ids.
Mutations are attributable and safe under parallel agent use.
No critical workflow requires hidden chat context or manual foreground interaction.
Argus can steer and re-observe all core controls.
verification: Parallel-agent mutation tests for selected workflows.
Manual-content tests for model operation guidance.

validation_evidence.proof_summary: Atelier model-operation routes now require valid lease context for model actors, canonical operator headers for operator bypass, session-bound renew/release, filesystem-health mutation guard coverage, backend action-receipt lease lineage enforcement, canonical native operator defaults, Facial Review backend-session thread binding, and honest prompt-feedback local-preview wording/manual coverage.

PASS: exit 0; Git reported LF-to-CRLF warnings only

adversarial_reviews.result: Findings addressed: MT-022 state drift, receipt test fields, operator spoofing bypass, session-bound renew/release, migration lineage, frontend no-lease bypass, Facial Review thread binding, stale lease state reads, and prompt-feedback persistence overclaim.

Findings addressed: filesystem-health mutation guard, native default actor consistency, receipt lineage DB/store enforcement, Facial Review session-id binding, and prompt-feedback local-preview manual/UI wording.

residual_risks: The local default managed PostgreSQL database has pre-existing migration checksum drift on migration 336; MT-022 action-receipt tests passed on a clean temporary database that was dropped after use.
Existing unrelated Rust warnings remain outside the MT-022 change surface.
No official validator verdict is claimed; validator_verdict remains PENDING.

Not run against the concurrent cluster to avoid disrupting an active session (data-loss/no-disruption rule). Backend proof binary COMPILES (compile-gate PASS, exit 0). Verdict basis: committed-presence-at-HEAD + backend compile-gate PASS + 5-agent adversarial committed-source review + coder's recorded managed-PG non-SKIP passes on this same cluster. Consistent with V1 (runtime_reexec then = ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED_HOST_OOM).
